en.p: For the function $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{3}x^{3}-x^{2}+\ln\left(1+x^{2}\right)+a$ ($a$ is a constant) and two positive numbers $b$, $c$, the function
is differentiable on the set of all real numbers. When $a+b+c=p+q\ln 2$, find the value of $30(p+q)$. (Here $p$ and $q$ are rational numbers, and $\ln 2$ is irrational.) [4 points]
